Commentary.Commentary: So, the result of this match means the points will be shared and South Africa regain the top spot. The table is still wide open and no team has officially booked their berth in the finals. Each game from hereon will be a must-win for everyone. We had a damp day today but we will be hoping that the conditions improve here at Barbados as the rest of the games will be played here including the finals. Australia will clash against the hosts West Indies on 21st June. Do join us to catch all the action. Until then, goodbye and good night! Cheers!

Update 1825 Local time - The inevitable has happened. It was raining all throughout and the match officials have decided to CALL IT OFF. We had just a single over and since then the rain gods took over the charge and never really stopped. The ground staff did their best to resume the play but that wasn't meant to be.

Update 1745 local time - Bad news! Just when the umpires were out for an inspection, it started to pour once again. At the same, the umpires feel that the pitch looks not at all safe to play. Stay tuned for the official confirmation. We may have a match or it maybe be called off anytime soon.

Update 1715 local time - After looking at the pitch, the umpires says that ground looks pretty okay but the center of the pitch is bit damped. So the next inspection will be at 1545. Stay tuned for the next update.
Update 1630 local time - Good news, folks! The drizzle has stopped and covers are coming off. We might have a game on our hands. Stay tuned for more updates.
Update 1441 local time - It is still raining heavily at Barbados.

Update 1310 local time - Oh dear! We have a rain affected game already. Just when we heard about the overcast conditions, the rains are here. Meanwhile, covers are racing onto the pitch and players are heading back to the pavilion. We might start losing overs after an hour.
Length ball outside off, Amla shoulders his arms.
Wide! Too full outside off, Amla lets it through and wide is given. This first over is never ending.
Yet another yorker ball on leg, it is flicked to square leg for a single.
The Floodlights are on already.
Too full in the blockhole, Quinton drills that well to square leg for no run.
Starc is little unhappy as he demands some sawdust to be sprinkled near landing area.
Wide! Too down the leg side, de Kock leaves that to be given as a wide. Wrong line there by Starc as he looks bit rusty.
Length ball on middle and leg, de Kock off his front foot looks to block that but gets a thigh pad to the leg side.
Full and on off, defended neatly by de Kock off the front foot.
FOUR! Driven away! Full and on off, tad of swing on that one. de Kock simply drives that through cover-point for a boundary. Great start with four.
Wide! First ball on its way! Starc bowls a bouncer. And oh, dear it is signaled as a wide. That ball went double the height of Quinton.
Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock will open the batting proceedings for South Africa. Mitchel Starc will have have a go with the new ball from Australia. Here we go, 3-2-1, let's play!
PITCH REPORT - Jeffrey Dujon feels that the pitch will have some pace and bounce and spinners will might miss the turn. On the weather, it should hold up.

AB DE VILLIERS Says that they would have bowled first too. About D/L, they will like to bowl well and put up a good game like last time. On his 200th ODI for SA, feels proud to play for the nation and would like to maintain that. On their final berth, it is possible if they play well like last game. Confirms only one change as Shamsi goes out and Morne Morkel comes in. Ends by wishing Happy Father's Day to all.

STEVEN SMITH about the pitch, he says that it looks a bit different and would like to bowl first. Further says as it might rain so would like to do well. On their tour, admits that it is going to be good. On their team changes, Head, Zampa and Coulter-Nile are out. Maxwell, Starc and Boland are in for them.
TOSS - Australia win the toss and elect to bowl first!

To sum it up, this game is of highest importance as the one winning tonight will almost book their berth for the finale. Can AB de Villiers thump the might of Steven Smith's playing XI? Or will we have a roaring comeback of Aussies to make their presence felt? Stay tuned for the all-important toss.

Hello and a warm welcome for the 7th match of this tri-series as we move into the third leg now and we have two powerhouse heading against each other. South Africa will take on Australia at Barbados. The Proteas are sitting at the top of the points table with their last win against the hosts with a bonus point. On the other hand, Australia will like to bounce back in this game after their humiliating defeat to West Indies.
